goal: Add tags, priorities, edit and remove to tasklist, keeping task files from earlier versions working and unchanged in output.
non_goals: No tag renaming, no tag listing command, no filtering by priority.
No migration or rewrite of old task files: missing keys are read as defaults and only written when a command changes that task.
No change to the add/done output, to the --file/TASKLIST_FILE handling, or to TASKLIST_TODAY.

acceptance_criteria.statement: `add TITLE --tag NAME` (repeatable) stores the tags on the new task as a JSON list under key "tags", in the order given with duplicates dropped; with no --tag no "tags" key is stored. A valid tag matches [a-z0-9-]+ (non-empty, ASCII only). If any tag is invalid, nothing is stored (the file is not created or changed), exit status is 2, and stderr is exactly one line of the form `error: invalid tag: VALUE` naming the offending value. Success still prints `added ID`.
acceptance_criteria.verification: test_cli tests running main() with --file and reading the JSON file back.

acceptance_criteria.statement: `tag ID NAME` adds NAME to the task's "tags" (creating the key if missing; already present is a no-op with exit 0) and prints `tagged ID`. `untag ID NAME` removes it, deletes the "tags" key when it becomes empty, and prints `untagged ID`; untagging a tag the task does not carry exits 2 with one stderr line. An unknown id exits 2 with one stderr line `error: no task with id ID`, changing nothing. An invalid NAME for `tag` exits 2 as in AC-1, changing nothing.
acceptance_criteria.verification: test_cli tests on the file contents, exit status and stderr line count.

acceptance_criteria.statement: `list` appends a task's tags to its line after the title and any due date, space separated, each as `#NAME`, e.g. `[ ] 1 Call Sam (due 2026-10-01) #work #home`; a task with no tags (or no "tags" key) gets no trailing text. `list --tag NAME` shows only tasks whose tags include NAME. It combines with --all (include done tasks carrying the tag) and with --overdue (only overdue tasks carrying the tag). An invalid NAME for --tag exits 2 with one stderr line `error: invalid tag: VALUE`.
acceptance_criteria.verification: test_cli tests comparing captured stdout line by line.

acceptance_criteria.statement: `add TITLE --priority high|normal|low` stores the value under key "priority"; with no option it stores "normal". Any other value exits 2 with one stderr line `error: invalid priority: VALUE` and nothing is stored. A task lacking the key is treated as normal everywhere.
acceptance_criteria.verification: test_cli tests on file contents and stderr.

acceptance_criteria.statement: `list` (with or without --all, --tag) orders the shown tasks by priority (high, normal, low) then by id. A high-priority task's line has `! ` (exclamation mark and one space) immediately before its title, i.e. `[ ] 3 ! Pay rent`; normal and low tasks have no marker. `list --overdue` keeps its existing oldest-due-first order regardless of priority, and still shows the `! ` marker on high tasks.
acceptance_criteria.verification: test_cli tests with mixed priorities and ids, comparing stdout order; core unit tests for the sort.

acceptance_criteria.statement: `edit ID [--title T] [--due DATE | --no-due] [--priority P]` changes only the given fields and prints `edited ID`. --no-due removes the "due" key. The title is stripped like in add. Exit 2 with one stderr line and the file unchanged when: the id is unknown (`error: no task with id ID`), the title is blank, the due date is not YYYY-MM-DD (`error: invalid due date: VALUE`), the priority is invalid (as AC-4), no field option is given, or --due and --no-due are both given. Tags, done state and id are never altered by edit. Validation of all values happens before any change, so a bad value alongside a good one changes nothing.
acceptance_criteria.verification: test_cli tests on file contents before and after; core unit tests for edit_task.

acceptance_criteria.statement: `remove ID` deletes the task from the file and prints `removed ID`. Other tasks are untouched and ids are not renumbered. An unknown id exits 2 with one stderr line `error: no task with id ID` and the file is unchanged.
acceptance_criteria.verification: test_cli tests on file contents; core unit test for remove_task.

acceptance_criteria.statement: A task file written by an earlier version (tasks with only id, title, done and optionally due) loads; `list`, `list --all`, `list --overdue`, `list --tag x`, `done` and `edit` work on it; its tasks print exactly as before (no marker, no tag text); `done` on it adds no "tags" or "priority" key, and `edit` adds only the keys it was asked to change.
acceptance_criteria.verification: test_cli tests with a hand-written 0.1.0-style JSON file, comparing stdout to the pre-change format and the JSON afterward.

interfaces.name: validate_tag
interfaces.signature: def validate_tag(name: str) -> str  # returns name; raises ValueError unless re.fullmatch(r'[a-z0-9-]+', name)

interfaces.name: PRIORITIES / validate_priority
interfaces.signature: PRIORITIES = ('high', 'normal', 'low'); def validate_priority(value: str) -> str  # raises ValueError

interfaces.name: Task
interfaces.signature: class Task(TypedDict): id, title, done, due: NotRequired[str], tags: NotRequired[list[str]], priority: NotRequired[str]

interfaces.name: add_task
interfaces.signature: def add_task(tasks, title, due=None, tags: list[str] | None = None, priority: str = 'normal') -> Task  # ValueError on bad input, before appending

interfaces.name: tag_task / untag_task
interfaces.signature: def tag_task(tasks, task_id: int, name: str) -> Task; def untag_task(tasks, task_id: int, name: str) -> Task  # KeyError unknown id; ValueError bad name (tag) or tag absent (untag)

interfaces.name: edit_task
interfaces.signature: def edit_task(tasks, task_id: int, title: str | None = None, due: str | None = None, no_due: bool = False, priority: str | None = None) -> Task  # KeyError unknown id; ValueError invalid value, nothing changed

interfaces.name: remove_task
interfaces.signature: def remove_task(tasks, task_id: int) -> Task  # KeyError unknown id

interfaces.name: visible_tasks
interfaces.signature: def visible_tasks(tasks, show_all: bool = False, tag: str | None = None) -> list[Task]  # priority then id order

interfaces.name: overdue_tasks
interfaces.signature: def overdue_tasks(tasks, today: datetime.date, tag: str | None = None) -> list[Task]  # existing order kept

interfaces.name: format_task
interfaces.signature: def format_task(task: core.Task) -> str  # '[ ] 3 ! Title (due D) #a #b'

interfaces.name: cmd_tag / cmd_untag / cmd_edit / cmd_remove
interfaces.signature: def cmd_X(args: argparse.Namespace, path: Path) -> int; subcommands tag ID NAME, untag ID NAME, edit ID [--title T] [--due D | --no-due] [--priority P], remove ID

interfaces.name: add and list options
interfaces.signature: add: --tag NAME (action=append), --priority VALUE; list: --tag NAME. Values validated in handlers (not argparse choices) so errors are one line `error: ...`

test_plan.scenario: add 'a' --tag work --tag home --tag work: file has tags ['work','home'], stdout 'added 1', exit 0. add 'b' with no tag: no 'tags' key.
add 'a' --tag Work (and 'a b', 'x_y', '', 'é'): exit 2, stderr is exactly one line containing the value, file does not exist / is unchanged. add 'a' --tag ok --tag BAD stores nothing.
add 'a'; tag 1 work -> 'tagged 1', tags ['work']; tag 1 work again exits 0, still one entry; untag 1 work -> 'untagged 1', no 'tags' key.
tag 9 work and untag 9 work on a file with only id 1: exit 2, one stderr line, file unchanged. untag 1 home when task has only work: exit 2. tag 1 BAD: exit 2, unchanged.
Tasks: 1 'a' tags work,home with due 2026-10-01; 2 'b' no tags. list prints '[ ] 1 a (due 2026-10-01) #work #home' then '[ ] 2 b'. list --tag home prints only task 1.

Done task 3 tagged work: list --tag work omits it, list --all --tag work includes it. With TASKLIST_TODAY=2026-10-05, list --overdue --tag work shows only overdue open tasks carrying work. list --tag BAD exits 2 with one stderr line.
add 'a' stores priority 'normal'; add 'b' --priority high stores 'high'; add 'c' --priority urgent exits 2, one stderr line naming 'urgent', file unchanged.
Tasks 1 low, 2 high, 3 normal, 4 high: list prints order 2, 4, 3, 1; lines for 2 and 4 read '[ ] 2 ! title'; others have no '!'. list --all orders done tasks by the same rule.
Overdue tasks 1 (due 2026-10-03, high) and 2 (due 2026-10-01, low), TASKLIST_TODAY=2026-10-05: list --overdue prints 2 then 1, task 1 with '! ' marker.

Task 1 'a' due 2026-10-01 tag work, priority normal. edit 1 --title ' b ' changes only title to 'b' (due, tags, priority kept), prints 'edited 1'. edit 1 --due 2026-11-01 changes due only. edit 1 --no-due drops the 'due' key. edit 1 --priority low changes priority only.

Each of edit 9 --title x; edit 1 --title '  '; edit 1 --due 2026-13-01; edit 1 --priority urgent; edit 1 (no options); edit 1 --due 2026-11-01 --no-due; edit 1 --title new --priority urgent exits 2 with one stderr line and leaves the file byte-identical.
Tasks 1,2,3: remove 2 prints 'removed 2', file holds 1 and 3 with unchanged content; a following add gets id 4. remove 9 exits 2, one stderr line, file unchanged.

Hand-written file [{'id':1,'title':'old','done':false},{'id':2,'title':'dated','done':false,'due':'2026-10-01'}]: list prints '[ ] 1 old' and '[ ] 2 dated (due 2026-10-01)' exactly; done 1 leaves task 1 with only id/title/done keys; edit 1 --title new changes only the title; list --overdue and list --tag x work (the latter prints nothing).

risks: Choices where the request was silent: the marker is '! ' with a space; tag/untag/edit print 'tagged ID', 'untagged ID', 'edited ID'; tag on an already-present tag is a no-op exit 0; untag of an absent tag exits 2; edit with no options exits 2; duplicates in repeated --tag are dropped keeping first-seen order; stored priority is written on add, but a missing key reads as normal.

Error text format 'error: ...' reuses the existing fail() helper; tests should check one-line stderr and the value named, but the exact wording is fixed above for invalid tag, invalid priority, invalid due date and no task with id.

argparse errors (e.g. --due with --no-due is validated in the handler, not via a mutually exclusive group, to keep stderr to one line; a non-integer ID still gets argparse's usage error with status 2).
list ordering by priority also applies with --all (done tasks sorted the same way); the request only states it for open tasks.
A malformed stored value (non-list tags, unknown priority string) in a hand-edited file is not validated beyond treating an unknown priority as normal; out of scope.
Because list --overdue keeps oldest-due-first, overdue_tasks must not be re-sorted by priority in cli.
split_proposal: Change 1 (size M): tags. Task.tags, validate_tag, add_task tags param, add --tag, tag/untag commands, list --tag (with --all/--overdue), tag text in format_task, plus tests for AC-1, AC-2, AC-3 and the tag part of AC-8. Branch `organize` from main.

Change 2 (size S/M): priorities. validate_priority, add --priority, priority-then-id ordering in visible_tasks, '! ' marker in format_task, overdue order untouched, plus tests for AC-4, AC-5 and the priority part of AC-8.
Change 3 (size M): edit and remove. edit_task, remove_task, edit/remove subcommands, plus tests for AC-6, AC-7 and the edit-on-old-file part of AC-8. Depends on change 2 for --priority validation.
